title: Checks that module layout uses only self named module files; bans mod.rs files.
summary: Having multiple module layout styles in a project can be confusing. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for modules that have the same name as their parent module
summary: A typical beginner mistake is to have mod foo; and again mod foo { .. } in foo.rs. The expectation is that items inside the inner mod foo { .. } are then available through foo::x, but they are only available through foo::foo::x. If this is done on purpose, it would be better to choose a more representative module name. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Detects public item names that are prefixed or suffixed by the containing public module’s name.
summary: It requires the user to type the module name twice in each usage, especially if they choose to import the module rather than its contents. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for modulo arithmetic.
summary: The results of modulo (%) operation might differ depending on the language, when negative numbers are involved. If you interop with different languages it might be beneficial to double check all places that use modulo arithmetic. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for getting the remainder of integer division by one or minus one.
summary: The result for a divisor of one can only ever be zero; for minus one it can cause panic/overflow (if the left operand is the minimal value of the respective integer type) or results in zero. No one will write such code deliberately, unless trying to win an Underhanded Rust Contest. Even for that contest, it’s probably a bad idea. Use something more underhanded. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.
